skill.name: geo-fundamentals
skill.description: Guide and checker for improving public web content for AI search citations in ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, and Gemini.
skill.summary: Helps teams assess and improve AI citation readiness for public web pages.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static finding is a false positive caused by Markdown inline code that documents a local Python command. The skill content and script focus on local GEO guidance and page checks, with no prompt injection or data exfiltration intent found.

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md line 155 uses Markdown backticks to document an optional local Python command. It is not Ruby or shell execution by the skill runtime, and the declared allowed tools are limited to Read, Glob, and Grep.

content.value_statement: AI search engines cite content that is clear, structured, and attributable. This skill helps teams review web pages for GEO readiness and practical improvements.
actual_capabilities: Explains GEO concepts and how they differ from traditional SEO.
Lists citation patterns across ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, and Gemini.
Provides checklists for author attribution, dates, schema, FAQs, and original data.
Documents AI crawler access considerations for common AI user agents.
Includes a local Python checker for HTML, JSX, and TSX public pages.
Scores likely public pages and reports missing GEO elements.
limitations: It does not verify live citations inside AI search engines.
The checker scans local files and does not crawl remote websites.
The script limits review to likely public HTML, JSX, and TSX pages.
Scores are heuristic and should be paired with editorial review.

use_cases.title: Improve AI Citation Readiness
use_cases.description: Review articles and landing pages for structure, attribution, dates, FAQs, and citable data.

use_cases.title: Compare SEO and GEO Priorities
use_cases.description: Translate traditional SEO work into GEO actions focused on entities, evidence, and extractable answers.

use_cases.title: Audit Pages Before Launch
use_cases.description: Run the local checker on public page files to find missing schema, headings, author details, and dates.

prompt_templates.title: Start a GEO Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one public page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this page for GEO readiness. Check headings, dates, author attribution, FAQs, and clear definitions.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Draft Article
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the GEO checklist to improve this article. Suggest changes that make it easier for AI engines to cite.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Structured Data
prompt_templates.scenario: Schema planning for a content team.
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend structured data for this page type. Include article, author, organization, and FAQ improvements where relevant.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a GEO audit on the public pages in this project. Summarize weak pages and prioritize fixes by citation impact.

output_examples.input: Audit a blog article for GEO readiness.
output_examples.output: The article has one clear H1 and an author name. Add publication dates, FAQ schema, and two sourced statistics.

output_examples.input: Review a product landing page for AI citation potential.
output_examples.output: The page explains the product well but lacks extractable definitions. Add comparison tables, named sources, and direct answers.

output_examples.input: Prioritize GEO fixes for a small site.
output_examples.output: Start with missing structured data and dates. Then add author credentials, FAQs, and original data to core pages.

best_practices: Use clear definitions and direct answers near the top of important pages.
Add author credentials, publication dates, and structured data to public content.
Support claims with named sources, original data, and concise comparison tables.
anti_patterns: Publishing thin pages without dates, authors, or source attribution.
Blocking AI crawlers without deciding how citations support business goals.
Treating GEO scores as final proof without manual content review.

faq.question: What is GEO?
faq.answer: GEO means Generative Engine Optimization. It improves the chance that AI search engines cite public content.

faq.question: Which AI engines does this skill discuss?
faq.answer: It covers ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, and Gemini, with notes on their citation patterns.

faq.question: Does the checker access the internet?
faq.answer: No. The included script checks local HTML, JSX, and TSX files in a project path.

faq.question: Can this guarantee AI citations?
faq.answer: No. It improves citation readiness, but AI engines choose sources using changing retrieval and ranking systems.

faq.question: What page elements matter most?
faq.answer: Clear headings, structured data, author details, dates, FAQs, definitions, and sourced statistics are important.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Content teams, SEO specialists, and developers can use it to improve public pages before publication.
